messages:
lucy: quick RFC follow-up — want to pin the capability negotiation direction for Hosted/Dedicated/Private. keeping this thread short to capture decisions and rollout steps.

devin: tl;dr: aim for one discovery pattern we can reliably test in e2e. probe endpoint vs static manifest: thoughts?

maria: agree on single pattern. my take: support both but with clear precedence. Private installers get a static manifest (air-gapped friendly). Hosted and Dedicated use a probe endpoint for dynamic capability signalling.

ashok: ok to support both. propose precedence: 1) local manifest present -> authoritative, 2) probe /internal/capabilities -> fallback, 3) default conservative capability set. Manifest avoids outbound dependency for Private.

lucy: good. tradeoffs to explicitly call out: manifest = simple offline install but operator config drift risk; probe = dynamic but requires auth and expands network surface.

devin: how to encode capabilities? booleans blow up. suggest a small schema with names + semantic version + optional params.

maria: exactly. capability descriptor: name, min_supported, optional params blob. keeps negotiation robust.

devin: example manifest snippet:
```
capabilities:
  - name: streaming_v2
    min_version: "2.0"
  - name: kv_cache
    min_version: "1.1"
    params: "max_prefix=256"
```

ashok: ops constraints: probe endpoint must require a signed ephemeral token (k8s SA JWT or control-plane-issued), be rate limited, and avoid verbose logs that might leak tenant topology.

lucy: also call out mismatches: KMS/HSM integrations are likely unavailable in Private; surface as capability flags so SDKs can fallback to local encryption.

maria: add capability "kms_external" with param types so clients know which fallback path to take.

devin: rollout proposal:
1) spec v1: manifest + probe + capability schema + examples.
2) SDK patch: read local manifest, else probe, return capabilities on client init.
3) runtime: gate features behind capability checks and emit telemetry when a requested capability is absent.
4) canary: Hosted 5% + one Dedicated cluster.

lucy: migration: compatibility-mode for old runtimes. default conservative behavior (core generation + embeddings only). add header `X-Rw-Capabilities: opt-in=v1` so older runtimes ignore it.

ashok: tests: fake-adapter in e2e to flip capabilities per test, and an offline manifest test for installer flows.

maria: ops checklist before canary: update deploy manifests, create PKI tokens for probe auth, update quickstart & examples. I'll own docs and examples.

devin: perf note: clients must cache capabilities with a TTL (5m default). avoid probing per-request.

lucy: log a warning if capabilities change mid-run (possible config drift). include telemetry event for capability transitions.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary job queued -> architecture-runtime/capability-probe -> job id 2026-09-14-88.

maria: will open the PR with spec + compatibility matrix. tagging @devin @ashok for review. :+1: :rocket:

devin: will review. add an explicit compatibility matrix (hosted/dedicated/private rows) in the spec for quick scanning.

lucy: agreed. final call: interface-first: spec + auth + schema, implementation flexible. short, actionable.
